GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_pedestrians_killed IS NULL) AS null_pk,
       SUM(number_of_pedestrians_killed) AS total_pk_all
FROM './data/crashes.parquet'
''').df())
"

input.content:
import duckdb
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import os

os.makedirs("out", exist_ok=True)

con = duckdb.connect()
df = con.sql("""
    SELECT YEAR(crash_date)::INT AS year,
           SUM(number_of_pedestrians_killed)::INT AS pedestrians_killed
    FROM './data/crashes.parquet'
    WHERE YEAR(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025
    GROUP BY 1
    ORDER BY 1
""").df()

df.to_csv("out/values.csv", index=False)
print(df.to_string(index=False))
print("Total 2013-2025:", df.pedestrians_killed.sum())

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
bars = ax.bar(df.year, df.pedestrians_killed, color="#C0392B", edgecolor="black", width=0.75)

mean = df.pedestrians_killed.mean()
ax.axhline(mean, ls="--", lw=1.5, color="#2C3E50",
           label=f"Mean: {mean:.0f} deaths/year")

for b, v in zip(bars, df.pedestrians_killed):
    ax.text(b.get_x() + b.get_width() / 2, v + 2, str(v),
            ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")

ax.set_title("Pedestrians Killed in NYC Motor Vehicle Crashes by Year, 2013–2025",
             fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("Pedestrians killed")
ax.set_xticks(df.year)
ax.set_ylim(0, max(df.pedestrians_killed) * 1.18)
ax.legend()
ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.3)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("out/initial.png", dpi=150)
print("Saved out/initial.png and out/values.csv")

part.text:
Checks passed: all 13 years are complete in the data (365/366 days each), no null dates or null values in `number_of_pedestrians_killed`, and no row where pedestrian deaths exceed total deaths. Chart and CSV saved to `./out/`.

ANSWER: Pedestrian deaths in NYC fell from a 13-year high of 176 in 2013 to 119 in 2025, averaging 130 per year. The decline was uneven: 2016 saw a rebound to 149, 2020 was the lowest year at 101 (101 deaths, ~29% below the 2013 peak), and the count has hovered in the 107–135 range since 2021.
